text.p: All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA) said on Thursday it waslaunching twice weekly Frankfurt to Osaka flights today.
Wataru Kubo, senior vice-president and general manager Europe, said the airline will fly Thursdays and Fridays using a Boeing 747-200 aircraft.
The outbound Germany flight originates in Rome and stops in Frankfurt, while the Wednesdays and Sundays inbound flight from Kansai airport continues on to Rome, he told a news conference.
ANA aims to handle 47,000 passengers and carry 802 tonnes of freight on the Frankfurt-Osaka route in the first year, Kubo said.
The airline decided not to offer first class seats on the Osaka route due to poor first class load factors on the Tokyo-Frankfurt route, he pointed out.
ANA carried 66,000 passengers on its three times a week B747-400 flights between Frankfurt and Tokyo in the 1995/96 fiscal year ending March 31, a rise of 13 percent, he added.
Up to 80 percent of these passengers originate in Japan, he said.
Kubo said ANA is held back from increasing Frankfurt-Tokyo flights because Narita Airport is full to capacity and slots cannot be obtained.
The airline plans to expand Kansai International Airport as a hub for Japan and neighbouring countries, he added.
With the new flight, ANA aims to achieve a 15 percent overall Japan-Germany market share behind Deutsche Lufthansa AG with 50 percent and Japan Airlines Co Ltd with 35 percent, Kubo said.
ANA General Manager, Germany, Mitsuhiko Shibata said the airline aims to raise its ex-Japan market share from 10 percent to 13 percent with the new Osaka flight.
German visitor numbers to Japan rose 5.6 percent to 68,317 last year while Japanese visitor numbers to Germany increased 11.4 percent to 233,711.
The Kansai region has a population of 25 million and generates one percent of the world's GNP, according to company information.

It is home to several large Japanese electronics manufacturers, banking and trading groups, which are all potential business travel clients, the airline noted. --Air Cargo Newsroom tel:+44 171 542 7706 fax:+44 171 542 5017
